target_customer: Parents of children and teens aged roughly 8 to 18 who pay per ride for a vetted driver
problem: Working parents cannot always shuttle kids to school and activities, and do not trust general rideshare apps with unaccompanied minors.
business_model: On-demand and scheduled kids ride service, per-ride fee priced above Uber or Lyft because of driver vetting

founders.name: Marta Jamrozik
prior_employers: A Fortune 500 company (not named in the source)
founders.background_notes: Dallas Innovates (2019-07-11) says she previously worked for a Fortune 500 company and lives in Connecticut. Education not found.

founders.name: Misha Laskin
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder with a current bio as a research scientist at DeepMind. His role at VanGo is not described in any other source I found.

competitors.name: HopSkipDrive
competitors.what: Los Angeles kids rideshare with vetted caregiver drivers
competitors.traction_then: named as a leading kids ride service in April 2016 coverage of Shuddle's closure
competitors.funding_then: not stated in the cited article

competitors.name: Zum
competitors.traction_then: named as a rival in April 2016 coverage
competitors.funding_then: not stated in the cited article

competitors.name: Kango
competitors.traction_then: named as a rival in April 2016 coverage
competitors.funding_then: not stated in the cited article

competitors.name: Shuddle
competitors.what: San Francisco Uber for kids that shut down
competitors.traction_then: ceased operations 2016-04-15 after failing to raise more

technical_complexity.rationale: A scheduling and dispatch app with GPS tracking and driver background checks. The hard parts were operational (fingerprinting, vehicle inspection, local driver supply) rather than technical.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded rivals offered the same service, and Shuddle's 2016 closure showed the model was hard to fund. Driver vetting was a process others could copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established by sources. Funded kids ride specialists such as Zum ($40M in 2019) and HopSkipDrive kept scaling while VanGo went inactive.

market_need_then: Parents cited trouble transporting kids and distrust of regular rideshare for minors; Shuddle, HopSkipDrive, Zum and Kango all existed by 2016, which shows demand but also that the market was crowded.

branding.name_origin: A local article reports the name was her husband's idea; no further origin story found
branding.domain_note: Used ridevango.com, not an exact vango.com match; the site is now an unpublished placeholder

identity.voice_and_tone: Parent-first safety messaging in press: fingerprinted drivers, GPS tracking, 85 percent of drivers are mothers

branding.community_and_virality: Local TV and newspaper coverage in Connecticut, Dallas and Houston in 2019; no sign of organic virality

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly name with local press, but no distinctive asset found, and a pun on van and Gogh that overlaps with other 'Van Go' businesses.

outcome_analysis: VanGo was a Y Combinator Winter 2017 company that did not launch its service until June 2018 in Connecticut, then expanded to the New York suburbs, Phoenix, Houston and Dallas by mid 2019. The YC directory now lists it as inactive, but no article or company notice explains when or why it stopped, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned. The sector context is that Shuddle shut in 2016 for lack of funding while Zum and HopSkipDrive raised larger rounds.
notes: The Entrepreneur and STN articles about a kids ride shutdown concern Shuddle (2016), not VanGo. Funding conflict: Dallas News (2019-07) cites Crunchbase for $270,000 seed from Y Combinator; CB Insights lists $150K seed dated 2019-03-19 and Dealroom a smaller figure. The $270,000 rests on one press mention of Crunchbase and is recorded undated. Company site ridevango.com is an empty hosting placeholder. YC lists Marta Jamrozik and Misha Laskin; Laskin's operating role is unconfirmed. Competitor funding_then not stated in the 2016 source; HopSkipDrive later raised $7.4M (CNBC 2017-11-21). Founded year not found.
